points.label: Covenant setting
points.left: Covenant memory appears before Moses returns to Egypt and before deliverance unfolds.
points.right: Covenant memory is explicitly connected to the unfolding Exodus rather than treated as an isolated ancestral event.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: Hear · remember · see · know · Israel · Abraham · Isaac · Jacob · Covenant memory · present slavery · Ancestral covenant
points.right: Yahweh remembers · Moses · Israel · Abraham · Isaac · Jacob · Bring out · redeem · take as people · bring into land · I will be your God

payload.posture: The narrative moves from hearing, remembering, seeing, and knowing to a public promise of rescue, peoplehood, and land.

rightEvidence.title: Covenant memory frames the Exodus promise

payload.tension: The two sources materially share covenant language or memory, while their parties, setting, action, or literary purpose remain distinct.
payload.title: God remembers / God announces rescue
